Calibrating the clocks. The temple bell is true. At dinner Odile says Félix's watch read 8:40 when the bell struck nine, so Félix's watch runs 20 minutes slow (true time = watch + 20). Dr Vauthier's watch is 2 minutes fast. Rosa's kitchen clock is 15 minutes fast. Girard's watch is 14 minutes slow, which is what their 10:29 piano report implies if the piano started at 10:43 true. Four witnesses (Dr Vauthier, Odile, Rosa, Lina) put the piano's start at 10:43 true, so that anchor is solid.

Félix's timeline in true time: someone went quickly up past the library at 10:35, the thump and the repeater came at 10:38, and someone came quickly down at 10:41. The repeater's pattern fits 10:38: ten hour notes, then two quarter notes, then eight minute notes. The repeater sounded when Monnier pressed the slide as he fell, so the blow was at 10:38.

Who was free at 10:35–10:41? Odile and Dr Vauthier were at piquet in the salon, each vouching for the other until 10:43. Lina and Rosa were in the kitchen together from 10:32, each vouching for the other. Félix was in the library and says he saw no one. That leaves Girard, who claims to have been in the street from 10:35 to 11:00.

Girard's account does not survive the honest witnesses. Félix saw Girard in the library at 10:32 by Félix's watch, which is 10:52 true, so Girard was back inside well before the 11:00 entry they claim. Girard's "faint bells at 10:34 by my watch" would be 10:48 true, which contradicts the repeater Félix heard at 10:38. Girard's "went out at 10:21 by my watch" falls at 10:35 true, the same moment someone was heard going up the stairs. Girard's cigar lit at 10:43 fits a descent at 10:41 and a step out to the street. Girard also had a motive: a quarrel over the repeater's price.

The manipulated clocks support this. The regulator was set back to a false 10:05 by the murderer's hand, though it was running at 10:20 per Lina. The hall clock was about 12 minutes fast at 10:00 and about 2 minutes fast at 10:58, so someone adjusted it in between. Girard was alone in the house and could have done both on the way up and down.

Residual inconsistencies I could not fully resolve: Lina's 10:20 departure against Rosa's 10:32 arrival, which implies Lina lingered on the way down, and the hall clock jump. Neither changes the answer. The alternative reading of 10:48 would require Félix's watch to be 30 minutes slow, which contradicts Odile's dinner account, and it would put the doctor in the hall at the moment the murderer had to pass him. I judge 10:38 by Girard to be the most consistent solution.
